attach-a-hook: Work attaches before or after a node, a phase or a step
A hook is one of four kinds
Each kind offers what the project actually has
A hook can be changed, moved or taken out
Hooks are written to the configuration in force
read-the-pipeline: The panel opens on the workflow the project runs now
The run reads left to right as steps, phases and nodes
Everything the project changed carries one mark
Hooks at one anchor read top to bottom in the order they run
A configuration the panel cannot read offers ways out
reshape-a-step: Saving an edit is what makes a node the project's own
A rewritten node can go back to the shipped one
A step's order and grouping are always written together
A node moves only when nothing downstream holds it
Nodes are taken out, put back and swapped without deleting anything
Phases are the project's to name, split and merge
A step's document is reshaped section by section
A project can add a step or hand one to a single document
switch-workflows-and-build: The header names the workflow in force and switches it
As shipped parks the project's configuration without deleting it
A new workflow starts from what runs now or from a shipped preset
Build and Preview build answer in the header
Every write says what it did, and the last one can be taken back where possible
The first open explains the board once
webview-safety: Text from outside is read as words, never as markup
record-a-run: Converge never changes a spec's status
release-the-spec-kit-extension: A setting written back leaves the rest of the file exactly as the person wrote it
